decisions.executionNote: Coin and bank are both in the left workspace. Begin a conservative elbow-up left-arm approach, raising before orienting down toward the holder.
Continue raised left approach toward the coin, progressively pitching the gripper downward while keeping the right arm parked.
The holder is visible in the left wrist view. Continue toward its overhead approach with small continuous rotations.
Move above the holder while completing most of the downward orientation; keep clearance before the final visual alignment.
Finish the vertical approach orientation above the estimated coin center; next use the wrist image to refine alignment before closing.
Wrist view shows the coin slightly right of the jaw center. Apply a small lateral correction and descend gradually while keeping the jaws open.
The wrist response shows the lateral correction had the opposite sign. Reverse it at fixed height to center the coin between the jaws.
The coin is now near the jaw center. Descend the final small distance and partially close, with a slight yaw correction to match the coin plane.
At grasp height the coin is slightly left of center after yawing. Make a small sideways correction without further descent or closing.
Coin is centered and aligned between the fingers. Close gently to the fully closed position, then inspect retention during lift.
Lift vertically with the left gripper closed. Check that the coin follows the fingers and separates from the holder.
The coin appears to remain with the holder rather than following the lift. Reopen and return for a slightly deeper, more centered grasp.
Descend another centimeter to engage more of the coin between the finger pads, correcting the small remaining lateral offset.
Close fully at the deeper centered grasp and allow the finger position to settle before testing the lift.
Test the second grasp with a slow two-centimeter vertical lift, keeping the gripper fully closed.
Continue the lift slowly to distinguish a retained coin from the holder; keep the jaws fully closed.
The coin now remains fixed between the fingers while the empty holder recedes. Lift beyond eight centimeters and begin moving toward the bank with clearance.
Raise the retained coin above the bank's top while translating left toward its slot; keep the downward grasp orientation.
Translate above the bank at clearance height, with the coin visibly retained. Approach the slot from the right without moving the parked arm.
Continue the level translation toward the slot; keep the coin elevated and the closed grasp unchanged.
The slot is just behind and slightly right of the retained coin in the wrist view. Refine the overhead alignment before descending.
The slot is visible and angled relative to the coin. Correct the yaw while lowering only two centimeters, then recheck precise alignment.
Coin and slot are nearly aligned. Apply the final small yaw and lateral correction while descending slowly toward insertion depth.
The coin is centered within the slot opening in the wrist view. Lower the last eight millimeters, then begin releasing without lateral motion.
Open fully at the aligned insertion position and let the coin settle into the bank before withdrawing.
Keep the hand stationary and fully open to allow release to complete; the coin still appears at the slot entrance.
Withdraw upward one centimeter with the open command maintained, allowing the fingertips to clear the slot without sideways drag.
The coin has disappeared into the aligned slot and the fingers are open. Withdraw from the bank and begin the continuous elbow-up return to origin.
Continue returning the empty left hand along a smooth raised retreat; make a tiny correction of the parked right arm back to its original pose.
Continue the smooth left-arm return, lowering only after clearing the bank and keeping both grippers open.
Return closer to the original left-arm position and orientation with continuous small increments; the holder is empty and no coin is visible outside the bank.
Slow the final approach to the original poses, preserving the same elbow-up branch and open grippers.
